title: Second Sound in Solids
authors: Marvin Chester
journal: Physical Review 131(5), 2013–2015
read_scope: All 3 PDF pages; first begins with final text of unrelated article
model_constitutive: Maxwell–Cattaneo relaxation: τ q_t+q=−K grad T; heat balance C T_t=−div q
geometry: Homogeneous rigid dielectric/insulating solid; bulk thermal waves
method: Macroscopic heat-flux and balance derivation, phonon-gas speed argument
main_result: Damped thermal wave, threshold frequency 1/(2πτ); estimated τ=3K/(C s²) and speed s/√3
validation: Low-frequency equation reduces to Fourier diffusion; the speed argument is compared to known phonon-gas theory, not an experimental validation
stated_limitations: No spatial pressure/density gradients; phonon-gas extension of kinetic arguments is hypothesized; τ estimate assumes phonon heat transport and idealized nondispersive isotropic speed; temperature loses meaning beyond equilibration rate
future_work: Authors report experiments underway, especially low-temperature KCl

title: Generalized thermoelasticity for anisotropic media
authors: Ranjit S. Dhaliwal; Hani H. Sherief
journal: Quarterly of Applied Mathematics 38(1), 1–8
read_scope: All 8 PDF pages
model_constitutive: Anisotropic local thermoelastic stress; Lord–Shulman-type single relaxation q_i+τ q̇_i=−k_ij θ_,j
geometry: General bounded anisotropic body; mixed displacement/traction and fixed-temperature boundary for uniqueness
method: Linear thermodynamic derivation, uniqueness energy argument, variational formulation
main_result: Anisotropic generalization; uniqueness under stated positivity and regularity; corresponding variational principle
validation: Analytic isotropic reduction to Lord–Shulman; no numerical or experimental validation
stated_limitations: Linearized theory near reference temperature; theorem assumes specified homogeneous data, regularity, positive density, heat capacity and elastic quadratic form; equations may contain PDF extraction errors
future_work: Not explicitly stated in inspected paper

title: Experimental Support for the Lagging Behavior in Heat Propagation
authors: Da Yu Tzou
journal: Journal of Thermophysics and Heat Transfer
read_scope: title, abstract, model section, conclusion (pp. 686-692)
model_constitutive: Rigid-conductor dual-phase-lag (DPL) heat conduction q(r, t + tau_q) = -K grad T(r, t + tau_T) with energy -div q = C_p dT/dt; Taylor-expanded to 1st/2nd order reducing to diffusion, CV-wave, Jeffreys, parabolic/hyperbolic two-step, and Guyer-Krumhansl limits.
geometry: 1D thin gold film (femtosecond laser heating) and 1D semi-infinite superfluid liquid helium (temperature pulse)
method: Laplace transform in time with analytical spatial solution and Riemann-sum numerical Laplace inversion
main_result: DPL reproduces ultrafast gold-film transient temperature response (with tau_q < tau_T, heat flux preceding temperature gradient due to phonon-electron coupling) and smooths CV wavefront corners into bell-shaped pulses matching liquid He II traces (with tau_T < tau_q).
validation: Quantitative comparison against femtosecond laser-heating experiments on gold films (Brorson et al. 1987; Qiu and Tien 1992; Qiu et al. 1994) and superfluid He II pulse oscilloscope traces (Bertman and Sandiford 1970); analytical reductions to 6 limiting models.
stated_limitations: Uses equilibrium temperature concept as an engineering approximation during ultra-short nonequilibrium transitions; general closed-form solution of exact delay PDE with unexpanded shifts tau_T, tau_q is not known.
future_work: Analyze physical cause-and-effect precedence (tau_T > tau_q vs tau_T < tau_q) across substructural delay mechanisms using the Boltzmann transport equation.

title: An Introduction to the Theory of Piezoelectricity (Second Edition)
authors: Jiashi Yang
journal: Advances in Mechanics and Mathematics Vol. 9 (Springer)
read_scope: frontmatter, TOC, Ch. 5 rod vibrations, Ch. 7 thermal/nonlocal/gradient effects, index (287 pp. monograph)
model_constitutive: 3D nonlinear electroelasticity (Tiersten two-continuum model) and IEEE-standard linear piezoelectricity; Ch. 7 adds linear/nonlinear thermopiezoelectricity, semiconduction, Eringen-type nonlocal dielectric kernel K(x-x') = (1/2alpha)exp(-|x-x'|/alpha) reduced on [0,h] to differential form, strain/polarization gradients, and full Maxwell coupling.
geometry: 3D general continua, rods, ceramic/quartz plates, cylinders, half-spaces, layered/jointed plates, thin dielectric film [0,h]
method: Variational principles, displacement-potential and four-vector formulations, harmonic plane/surface/guided wave eigenproblems, Fredholm integral-to-ODE reduction for bounded nonlocal thin film
main_result: Unified textbook derivation of 3D nonlinear/linear piezoelectricity, biasing-field incremental theory, exact wave/vibration solutions, and bounded-domain nonlocal thin-film capacitance C/C0 < 1 showing boundary-layer field enhancement near electrodes.
validation: Analytical recovery of local/classical limits (e.g., C/C0 -> 1 as h/alpha -> infinity, classical Rayleigh/Love/Bleustein-Gulyaev limits).
stated_limitations: Scope explicitly restricted mainly to exact 3D piezoelectric theory without pre-existing fields in Chs. 2-5; 1D/2D structural beam/plate/shell approximations deferred to other monographs.
future_work: Extensions beyond Ch. 1 framework (thermal, dissipative, semiconducting, nonlocal, gradient, full electromagnetic couplings) introduced only as brief introductory formulations in Ch. 7.

title: The Linear Theory of Micropolar Thermoelasticity
authors: T. R. Tauchert; W. D. Claus Jr.; T. Ariman
journal: International Journal of Engineering Science
read_scope: full paper (pp. 37-47)
model_constitutive: Linear isotropic and anisotropic micropolar thermoelasticity (Eringen micropolar balance laws + Clausius-Duhem inequality + Fourier heat law q_i = k theta_,i); couple stress m_kl independent of temperature in linear isotropic case.
geometry: General 3D bounded regular domain D with boundary B
method: Coleman-Noll thermodynamic restriction, displacement-microrotation (7 PDEs) and stress-couple-stress (19 unknowns + Sandru compatibility) formulations, energy-integral uniqueness proofs, body-force analogy, Goodier-type potential reduction
main_result: Constructs linear micropolar thermoelastic constitutive and field equations, proves uniqueness for coupled dynamic and uncoupled quasistatic BVPs, extends Duhamel-Neumann body-force analogy, and reduces uncoupled problems to isothermal micropolar elasticity via Poisson equations.
validation: Reduces to isothermal micropolar elasticity (Eringen 1966) when theta=0 and to classical linear thermoelasticity when coupling modulus kappa=0.
stated_limitations: Linear constant-property theory with classical Fourier conduction (infinite thermal speed); thermomechanical coupling neglected in sections 3.2-5 except where thermoelastic dissipation is primary.
future_work: Solve particular boundary-value problems including temperature effects to suggest experimental tests confirming or disproving micropolar thermoelasticity in granular media.

title: Wave reflection by the free boundary of a microstructured flexoelectric half-space
authors: Baljeet Singh; Geetika Gupta
journal: Mechanics Based Design of Structures and Machines
read_scope: title, abstract, governing equations (pp. 1-3), numerical results & conclusion (pp. 10-23)
model_constitutive: 2D centrosymmetric isotropic dielectric with strain-gradient elasticity (length scale l), micro-inertia -(1/3)rho_0 n^2 grad^2 u_tt, polarization gradients (a_12, a_44, a_77), and direct/converse static bulk flexoelectricity (f^d, f^c); isothermal (no thermal field).
geometry: 2D semi-infinite half-space (x3 >= 0) with stress-free plane boundary
method: Harmonic plane-wave ansatz reducing 4 coupled PDEs (u, w, P1, P3) to quadratic dispersion in V*^2; analytical reflection amplitude ratios and energy flux shares for incident qP and qSV waves
main_result: Identifies two dispersive plane waves (qP, qSV) slowed by micro-inertia and bulk flexoelectricity; reflected qP wave vanishes beyond critical qSV incidence angle theta_c = 28 deg; kl, n/l, and flexoelectricity strongly affect qP reflection near 60-70 deg.
validation: Energy conservation check (sum of reflected energy ratios <= 1 at all incident angles) and qualitative agreement with Qi (2019) for strontium titanate parameters.
stated_limitations: Restricted to 2D isothermal isotropic centrosymmetric half-space with static bulk flexoelectricity; for incident qSV wave, kl, n/l, and f have negligible effect on reflection/energy ratios.
future_work: None explicitly stated beyond nanoscale flexoelectric device/characterization relevance.

title: Propagation and attenuation of Rayleigh waves in generalized thermoelastic media
authors: M. D. Sharma
journal: Journal of Seismology
read_scope: title, abstract, intro, fundamental equations (pp. 61-64), conclusions & references (pp. 77-79)
model_constitutive: Unified 3D/2D isotropic generalized thermoelasticity covering Lord-Shulman (epsilon=1, single relaxation tau_0) and Green-Lindsay (epsilon=0, two relaxations tau_1 >= tau_0 >= 0) via Helmholtz potentials.
geometry: 2D/3D homogeneous isotropic half-space (z >= 0) with stress-free isothermal or thermally insulated plane boundary
method: Currie-type polynomial rationalization of complex irrational secular dispersion equation, numerical root-finding with radiation/decay filtering to remove spurious roots, depth-dependent particle-motion polarization analysis
main_result: Exact complex roots yield phase speed, attenuation, and elliptical/tilted particle trajectories for copper and limestone; insulated boundary can cause rectilinear surface motion and large changes in attenuation; no second (additional) thermoelastic Rayleigh mode found.
validation: Filters extraneous polynomial roots against original radical secular equation and depth-decay radiation condition; checks low/high-frequency behavior across copper and limestone.
stated_limitations: Homogeneous isotropic linear thermoelasticity only; unlike viscoelasticity (Currie et al. 1977), no additional Rayleigh surface wave root was found for the chosen thermoelastic models.
future_work: Investigate existence of additional Rayleigh surface waves in thermoviscoelastic materials using the rationalized dispersion framework.

title: Heat waves
authors: D. D. Joseph; Luigi Preziosi
journal: Reviews of Modern Physics
read_scope: title, abstract, TOC, Secs. I-II (pp. 41-43), Sec. VIII-IX concluding remarks & references (pp. 69-73)
model_constitutive: Comprehensive review of linear/nonlinear rigid-conductor heat-wave constitutive laws: Cattaneo telegraph law, Jeffreys-type effective thermal conductivity + memory kernel q = -k1 grad theta - int Q(t-t') grad theta dt', Guyer-Krumhansl, Gurtin-Pipkin internal-energy/heat-flux memory, Coleman-Fabrizio-Owen nonlinear Cattaneo.
geometry: Rigid heat conductors (1D pulses, half-space sudden heating, melt interfaces, dielectric crystals, liquid He II)
method: Boltzmann/kinetic, viscoelastic-analogy relaxation-kernel, random-walk, thermodynamic, and canonical wave/characteristic analyses plus annotated historical bibliography
main_result: Shows how fast-relaxing modes create an effective Fourier conductivity that singularly perturbs slower heat waves, explaining why diffusion dominates except at cryogenic second-sound windows (He II, NaF, Bi) or sub-relaxation timescales.
validation: Analytical canonical solutions and synthesis against classical cryogenic second-sound experiments (Peshkov, Ackerman, McNelly, Narayanamurti-Dynes) and MD shock studies (Tsai-MacDonald).
stated_limitations: Confined primarily to rigid conductors (deformations set to zero); notes that almost nothing is known about history dependence of internal energy and room-temperature relaxation times are too short for contemporaneous oscilloscopes.
future_work: Resolve melt-interface temperature jump vs singular Renardy-type kernels in Gurtin-Pipkin hyperbolic Stefan problems; measure history dependence of internal energy and ultra-short-time wave speeds.

title: A Higher-Order Nonlocal Elasticity and Strain Gradient Theory and Its Applications in Wave Propagation
authors: C. W. Lim; G. Zhang; J. N. Reddy
journal: Journal of the Mechanics and Physics of Solids
read_scope: title, abstract, intro (pp. 1-6), thermodynamic model derivation (pp. 8-10), MD comparison & conclusions (pp. 25-31)
model_constitutive: Higher-order nonlocal strain gradient elasticity (NSGT): stored energy depends nonlocally on both strain epsilon_kl (kernel alpha_0, parameter e0*a) and first strain gradient epsilon_kl,m (kernel alpha_1, parameter e1*a) plus material gradient length l; isothermal.
geometry: 3D continuum specialized to 1D Euler-Bernoulli and Timoshenko nanobeams (carbon nanotubes)
method: Thermodynamic/Clausius-Duhem framework with Polizzotto nonlocal residuals, variational derivation of higher-order PDEs and BCs, analytical harmonic flexural dispersion relations
main_result: Unifies softening Eringen nonlocal stress and stiffening strain-gradient effects into one differential beam dispersion law with critical and cut-off wavenumbers, capturing both long-wavelength stiffness enhancement and high-wavenumber phase-velocity roll-off.
validation: Exact reductions to pure Eringen nonlocal stress (l=0) and pure strain-gradient elasticity (e0=e1=0); quantitative dispersion benchmarked against CNT molecular dynamics (MD) data of Liew et al. (2008).
stated_limitations: Isothermal linear beam wave analysis; requires cut-off wavenumber (~10 nm^-1) at very high wavenumbers where phase velocity drops sharply.
future_work: Apply higher-order nonlocal strain-gradient framework to broader nanostructure mechanics (shells, plates, BCs) beyond 1D CNT beam wave dispersion.

title: Nonlocal elasticity of Klein-Gordon type: fundamentals and wave propagation
authors: Markus Lazar; Eleni Agiasofitou
journal: Wave Motion
read_scope: title, abstract, Secs. 1-2 (pp. 1-8), Sec. 4 dispersion/velocities (pp. 18-19), Sec. 5 conclusions & Appendix A (pp. 22-31)
model_constitutive: 3D linear elasticity with separable space-time nonlocality t_ij = alpha(x,t) * sigma_ij(x,t), where weak nonlocal operator is the Klein-Gordon operator L = 1 - l^2 Laplacian + (l^2/c^2) d^2/dt^2 (4 parameters: lambda, mu, length l, nonlocal speed c or time tau=l/c); isothermal.
geometry: 3D unbounded homogeneous isotropic elastic continuum
method: Green's function derivation of retarded Klein-Gordon dynamical kernels in 1D/2D/3D, Fourier transform dispersion analysis yielding quadratic in omega^2 for longitudinal and transverse waves
main_result: Fourth-order time derivative arises naturally from Klein-Gordon space-time nonlocality, predicting both acoustic (LA, TA) and positive-group-velocity optic (LO, TO) branches separated by a frequency band-gap using only 3 displacement DOFs and 4 parameters, provided c_L < c.
validation: Recovers Eringen Helmholtz spatial nonlocal elasticity as c -> infinity (tau -> 0) and classical elasticity as l -> 0; proves real positive omega^2 for all real k iff c_j < c (Appendix A).
stated_limitations: Restricted to unbounded isothermal homogeneous elastic continua; initial-boundary value problems and finite-domain modified kernels explicitly declared out of scope.
future_work: Initial-boundary value problems, finite-domain kernels, and anisotropic/coupled-field extensions (not solved in this paper).

title: Electromagnetic Waves Propagation in Graphene Multilayered Structures
authors: Mohammed M. Shabat; Muin F. Ubeid
journal: Journal of Electrical & Electronic Systems
read_scope: full paper (pp. 1-5)
model_constitutive: Macroscopic linear Maxwell equations for s-polarized (TE) monochromatic electromagnetic waves; graphene modeled as thin lossy dielectric slab of thickness d_g = N_g * 0.34 nm with complex refractive index n_g = 3 + i(C/3)lambda (C = 5.446 um^-1); no mechanics or heat.
geometry: 1D N-period graphene/dielectric (CaF2) multilayer stack embedded between vacuum half-spaces under oblique TE incidence
method: Snell's law, tangential E/H interface matching, Fresnel coefficients, and Vigoureux recursive transfer relation
main_result: Computes reflectance R', transmittance T', and graphene loss power P_loss = 1 - R' - T' vs wavelength (100-1700 nm), incidence angle, CaF2 thickness, and graphene layer count (1-3 monolayers).
validation: Energy conservation identity R' + T' + P_loss = 1 checked across all numerical examples.
stated_limitations: Purely optical/electromagnetic TE multilayer calculation using empirical visible-range refractive index for graphene; no thermoelastic or mechanical coupling.
future_work: Potential use in optical filters/biosensors hinted at end of conclusions.

title: A Note on Non-simple Heat Conduction
authors: Peter J. Chen; Morton E. Gurtin; William O. Williams
journal: Zeitschrift fur angewandte Mathematik und Physik (ZAMP)
read_scope: full paper (pp. 969-970)
model_constitutive: Steady-state linearized Chen-Gurtin two-temperature rigid heat conductor: q = -k grad phi, theta = phi - a Laplacian phi (isotropic, a > 0) and centrosymmetric anisotropic counterpart q = -K grad phi, theta = phi - lambda K : grad grad phi.
geometry: 3D rigid conductor (with 1D experimental slab/bar specialization noted)
method: Direct algebraic elimination between div q = r and two-temperature relation
main_result: Proves that in steady state the difference between thermodynamic and conductive temperatures is directly proportional to external heat supply: theta - phi = (a/k) r (or lambda r in anisotropic centrosymmetric media), vanishing when r = 0.
validation: Recovers theta = phi when external heat supply r = 0.
stated_limitations: Restricted to time-independent (steady-state) rigid heat conductors.
future_work: Suggests 1D steady controllable-radiation experiment to detect whether the two-temperature discrepancy a > 0 exists physically.

title: On the Thermodynamics of Non-simple Elastic Materials with Two Temperatures
authors: Peter J. Chen; Morton E. Gurtin; William O. Williams
journal: Zeitschrift fur angewandte Mathematik und Physik (ZAMP)
read_scope: full paper (pp. 107-112)
model_constitutive: Nonlinear and linearized two-temperature thermoelasticity (Chen-Gurtin-Williams): nonlinear response depends on F, VF, VVF and phi, Vphi, VVphi; linearized isotropic theory has S = lambda(tr E)I + 2mu E - alpha(3lambda+2mu)(phi - phi_0 - a Laplacian phi)I, q = -k grad phi, theta = phi - a Laplacian phi.
geometry: General 3D elastic body, specialized to steady free expansion of a cylinder of length l under uniform radiation r
method: Modified two-temperature Clausius-Duhem inequality (Coleman-Noll exploitation) and infinitesimal linearization
main_result: Shows two temperatures permit higher-grade dependence thermodynamically, yet linearized isotropic theory is mechanically simple (no strain gradients) and yields coupled PDEs where steady heat supply r induces an extra pressure p = beta*r and volume-change offset.
validation: Reduces to classical linear thermoelasticity when temperature discrepancy a = 0 (or steady r = 0).
stated_limitations: Proofs of nonlinear thermodynamic theorems omitted as analogous to Chen-Gurtin (1968); linearized theory remains parabolic/mechanical-simple without finite thermal wave speed.
future_work: Proposes steady-state radiation-induced free volume expansion of a cylinder as an experimental way to measure temperature discrepancy a.

title: On the Clausius-Duhem Inequality
authors: Morton E. Gurtin; William O. Williams
journal: Zeitschrift fur angewandte Mathematik und Physik (ZAMP)
read_scope: full paper (pp. 626-633)
model_constitutive: Axiomatic continuum thermodynamics with modified two-temperature Second Law d/dt int eta dm >= int (r/phi) dm - int (q.n/theta) da, tested on 'thermally regular' local constitutive classes and simple materials with fading memory.
geometry: General 3D deformable continuum B
method: Axiomatic measure-theoretic formulation and Coleman-Noll-type variational/Frechet-derivative contradiction proof
main_result: Proves that for any thermally regular constitutive class—including simple elastic materials with fading memory—compatibility with the two-temperature Second Law forces surface temperature theta and volume temperature phi to be identical, recovering the classical Clausius-Duhem inequality.
validation: Logical recovery of classical single-temperature Clausius-Duhem inequality for simple materials.
stated_limitations: Applies to thermally regular/simple materials; non-simple materials depending on higher spatial gradients violate thermal regularity and can sustain theta != phi.
future_work: Points to forthcoming full axiomatic paper (Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal. 1967) and motivates non-simple two-temperature theories.

title: On a Theory of Heat Conduction Involving Two Temperatures
authors: Peter J. Chen; Morton E. Gurtin
journal: Zeitschrift fur angewandte Mathematik und Physik (ZAMP)
read_scope: title, intro, thermodynamic derivation & linearization (pp. 614-621), example plots & references (pp. 625-627)
model_constitutive: Rigid non-simple two-temperature heat conductor: e, s, theta, q depend on (phi, grad phi, grad^2 phi); linearized isotropic PDE c phi_t = k Laplacian phi + c*a Laplacian phi_t + r with theta = phi - a Laplacian phi (k > 0, a >= 0).
geometry: 3D rigid heat conductor; canonical progressive waves, acceleration/discontinuity fronts, and 1D semi-infinite bar under step boundary temperature
method: Coleman-Noll exploitation of two-temperature entropy inequality, material-symmetry tensor representation, energy uniqueness proof, harmonic/discontinuity analysis, Laplace/analytical step-heating solution
main_result: Proves A(phi) = lambda(phi) K(phi) >= 0; spatial derivative jumps in e and q decay exponentially as exp(-kt/(ca)) rather than vanishing instantaneously, and backward-in-time problem is stable for a > 0.
validation: Recovers classical Fourier heat equation as temperature discrepancy a -> 0 (shown in Figs. 2-3 for semi-infinite bar).
stated_limitations: Rigid heat conductor only (no elastic deformation); third-order mixed derivative Laplacian phi_t still gives non-hyperbolic propagation.
future_work: Extension to deformable thermoelastic materials (carried out in Chen, Gurtin & Williams 1969).

title: On surface waves in generalized thermoelasticity
authors: V. K. Agarwal
journal: Journal of Elasticity
read_scope: full paper (pp. 171-177)
model_constitutive: 3D homogeneous isotropic linear generalized thermoelasticity of Lord-Shulman (relaxation tau) and Green-Lindsay (two constants alpha >= alpha* > 0) with surface thermal radiation BC theta_,3 + h*theta = 0.
geometry: 3D homogeneous isotropic half-space (x3 >= 0) with traction-free, radiating/isothermal/insulated plane boundary
method: Extension of Knowles (1966) and Carroll (1974) Lame-potential surface-wave representation theorem for general (non-plane) harmonic surface waves
main_result: Proves free harmonic thermoelastic surface waves in LS and GL half-spaces are governed by a single 2D surface wave potential satisfying the 2D Helmholtz equation, yield elliptical particle paths in spatially varying planes, and share identical secular equations when alpha = alpha* = tau.
validation: Reduces to Carroll (1974) classical thermoelastic surface waves when tau = 0 (or alpha = alpha* = 0), to Nayfeh & Nemat-Nasser (1971) when h = 0, and to classical Rayleigh equation when epsilon = 0.
stated_limitations: Analytical secular equation derived and compared structurally, without numerical root-finding across parameter regimes.
future_work: None explicitly stated.

title: Thermodynamics with Internal State Variables
authors: Bernard D. Coleman; Morton E. Gurtin
journal: The Journal of Chemical Physics
read_scope: title, abstract, Secs. 1-3 (pp. 597-599), Sec. 14 ideal-gas example & conclusion (p. 613)
model_constitutive: Nonlinear thermoelastic continua with N internal ('hidden') state variables alpha = (alpha_1,...,alpha_N) governed by ODEs dot(alpha) = f(theta, F, grad theta, alpha) alongside psi, eta, T, q depending on (theta, F, grad theta, alpha).
geometry: General 3D nonlinear deformable heat-conducting body (and ideal gas with internal vibrational mode)
method: Coleman-Noll Clausius-Duhem exploitation, Lyapunov/nonlinear ODE asymptotic stability theory at fixed (F, theta), integral dissipation inequalities
main_result: Establishes thermodynamic identities T = rho d_F psi, eta = -d_theta psi, d_grad_theta psi = 0, internal dissipation d_alpha psi . f <= 0, Lyapunov role of free energy at equilibrium, conditions for internal-mode temperatures, and relaxing ideal-gas specialization.
validation: Recovers classical thermostatics at internal equilibrium and classical relaxing polyatomic ideal-gas vibrational relaxation equations (Bethe-Teller/Landau-Teller).
stated_limitations: Finite internal state variables yield discrete relaxation spectra when linearized (less suited than fading-memory functionals for broad polymer spectra); body couples and mass diffusion excluded.
future_work: Foundation for internal-variable theories of dissipation, relaxation, and generalized heat/viscoplastic models.

title: Propagation of shear waves in an irregular magnetoelastic monoclinic layer sandwiched between two isotropic half-spaces
authors: A. Chattopadhyay; S. Gupta; A. K. Singh; S. A. Sahu
journal: International Journal of Engineering, Science and Technology
read_scope: title, abstract, formulation (pp. 228-232), numerical plots & conclusion (pp. 240-244)
model_constitutive: Perfectly conducting linear magnetoelastic monoclinic crystal layer (Lorentz body force J x B, linearized Maxwell stress, sigma -> infinity, displacement current neglected) between two isotropic elastic half-spaces; isothermal.
geometry: 2D/antiplane sandwiched monoclinic layer (-H <= y <= epsilon*h(z)) with small rectangular lower-interface irregularity between two isotropic elastic half-spaces
method: Fourier transform, Eringen-Samuels (1959) first-order boundary perturbation in epsilon = H'/s << 1, contour integration
main_result: Closed-form perturbed Love-type SH dispersion relation showing phase velocity c/beta_2 decreases as rectangular irregularity depth H'/H or magnetoelastic monoclinic parameter m_H increases.
validation: Reduces to classical isotropic Love-type sandwiched-layer dispersion relation when magnetic field, monoclinic anisotropy, and interface irregularity vanish.
stated_limitations: First-order perturbation valid only for small irregularity aspect ratio epsilon = H'/s << 1, perfectly conducting assumption (sigma -> infinity), isothermal SH polarization only.
future_work: Geophysical seismic interpretation across irregular crustal/continental-margin layers.

title: Reflection and Transmission of Elastic Waves at Viscous Liquid/Micropolar Elastic Solid Interface
authors: Rajneesh Kumar; Sushil K. Tomar
journal: International Journal of Mathematics and Mathematical Sciences
read_scope: full paper (pp. 685-694)
model_constitutive: 2D linear Eringen micropolar elastic solid (potentials phi, U, Phi; longitudinal wave and two coupled transverse-microrotation waves for omega^2/omega_0^2 > 2) welded to compressible Navier-Stokes viscous liquid; isothermal.
geometry: Plane interface z = 0 separating viscous liquid half-space (z < 0) and isotropic micropolar elastic half-space (z > 0)
method: Helmholtz potential decomposition, Snell's law, 5x5 complex linear interface BC system solved numerically for reflection/refraction amplitude ratios
main_result: Computes amplitude ratios Z1..Z5 vs incidence angle (0-90 deg) for incident longitudinal or coupled transverse-microrotation waves, demonstrating measurable liquid-viscosity effects on reflected/refracted amplitudes.
validation: Reduces analytically to inviscid-liquid/micropolar-solid interface solution of Tomar & Kumar (1995) when viscosity eta -> 0; uses Gauthier aluminum-epoxy micropolar data.
stated_limitations: Isothermal 2D plane-harmonic analysis; energy-flux conservation balance across the dissipative viscous interface is not checked.
future_work: Potential application to water-mud-rock or crust-mantle seismological interfaces.

title: Bleustein-Gulyaev waves in some functionally graded materials
authors: Bernard Collet; Michel Destrade; Gerard A. Maugin
journal: European Journal of Mechanics A/Solids
read_scope: title, abstract, Secs. 1-3 (pp. 695-698), Secs. 4-5 & references (pp. 704-706)
model_constitutive: Quasi-electrostatic linear piezoacoustics in a functionally graded 6mm hexagonal piezoelectric half-space with co-proportional depth grading {c44, e15, eps11, rho}(x2) = {c44^0, e15^0, eps11^0, rho^0} f(x2); isothermal.
geometry: Semi-infinite 6mm piezoelectric half-space (x2 >= 0) with traction-free electrically free or metallized surface
method: Liouville-type rescaling u_hat = sqrt(f) u decoupling 4x4 first-order system into constant-coefficient 2nd-order ODEs, plus Varley-Seymour hierarchy generating infinitely many exact solvable profiles f(x2)
main_result: Derives exact closed-form Bleustein-Gulyaev surface-wave speed, depth profiles, and electromechanical coupling K_S^2 for exponential, algebraic (beta*x2+1)^+-2, hyperbolic/trigonometric, and asymptotically homogeneous tanh^2 profiles.
validation: Recovers classical homogeneous Bleustein-Gulyaev (1968/1969) solution as grading parameter beta -> 0 (PZT-4 ceramic examples).
stated_limitations: Explicitly notes that proportional grading of mass density rho(x2) alongside c44, e15, eps11 is physically restrictive/unlikely, adopted so exact elementary-function benchmarks exist; isothermal anti-plane SH only.
future_work: Use exact analytical solutions as benchmarks for BEM/numerical solvers when density and stiffness/piezoelectric moduli have independent depth profiles.
